chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) whether the people of Mecca should perform Tamattu', so he said, 'No, the people of Mecca do not perform Tamattu'.' I said, 'And those who reside in it?' He said, 'If they reside for a year or two years, they do as the people of Mecca do; but if they reside for a month, then they have the right to perform Tamattu'.' I said, 'From where?' He said, 'They exit the Haram.' I said, 'From where do they enter the Ihram for Hajj?' He said, 'From Mecca, approximately as the people say.'

The Shaykh (peace be upon him) said: The description of Tamattu' ('Umrah to Hajj') is that the pilgrist enters the Ihram for 'Umrah from the Miqat. When he enters Mecca, he performs Tawaf around the House seven times and Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah seven times, then he releases himself from Ihram from whatever he had entered Ihram for. When it is the Day of Tarwiyah at the time of the sun's decline, he enters the Ihram for Hajj from the Masjid Al-Haram. Upon him are two Tawafs around the House, which are added to the first one, and another Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, which is added to his previous Sa'i. Thus, the obligatory Tawaf upon him around the House for Hajj and 'Umrah becomes three Tawafs, and the obligatory Sa'i is two Sa'is, and upon him is a Dam (sacrifice) which he must shed; he has no choice but to do that.

key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs 'Umrah first, then Hajj)
key_terms.الْقَارِنُونَ: Those who combine 'Umrah and Hajj together (Qiran)
key_terms.سَعْيٌ آخَرُ: Another Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.يُهِلُّونَ: They enter the state of Ihram (reciting Talbiyah)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for Mecca residents to perform Tamattu' and what are its specific ritual requirements?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction for Mecca's residents regarding Hajj rituals, establishing that long-term residents (those staying one to two years) are treated as locals who do not perform *Tamattu'*, while short-term residents must exit the *Haram* boundary to do so. It further details the specific ritual obligations of *Tamattu'*, requiring three Tawafs and two Sa'is, along with the mandatory *Dam* (sacrifice), reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise adherence to ritual boundaries and compensatory acts.
